topBullish.label: Volatility

metrics.label: Trend Strength
metrics.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.01 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.
metrics.explanation: Over 60 sessions DIA moved +0.3%, and only 1% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.
metrics.whyItMatters: Direction alone does not say whether a move is worth following. The same net return produced by a straight line and by a round trip demand different trades; efficiency is what separates them.
conflicts: Net move is positive but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
metrics.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.01 now

metrics.label: Market Structure
metrics.confidenceBasis: 10 swing highs and 14 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 12% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
metrics.explanation: DIA is printing lower highs and higher lows — compressing into a coil. Last swing high 519.67 vs prior 535.58; last swing low 515.52 vs prior 510.91.
metrics.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
conflicts: Range is narrowing; structure resolves on the break, and gives no direction until it does.
metrics.nextTrigger: resolves on a close outside 515.52–519.67

metrics.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are lagging safe government bonds by 3.6% — money is retreating into safety, the classic defensive move.
metrics.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 3% of them

categories.label: Risk & Volatility
categories.topReason: Volatility: IWM typically moves 1.33% in a day right now — more volatile than 9% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.

metrics.label: Volatility
metrics.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
metrics.explanation: IWM typically moves 1.33% in a day right now — more volatile than 9% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.
metrics.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
metrics.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 9% of them
